title: AI-Assisted Mathematical Results and Their Engineering Translation: An Evidence-Graded Review with Illustrative Electrical Engineering Numerical Studies
content: This evidence-graded narrative review examines 51 AI-assisted mathematical findings, representing 49 distinct target families, including published theorems, formal proof artefacts, counterexamples, bounds, constructions and unverified announcements. Mathematical result type, evidence level and engineering relevance are classified separately; recent preprints are distinguished from established results. Four electrical engineering pathways are investigated: numerical-radius and matrix-polynomial certificates for inverter control, preconfigured protection cycles for resilient communications, complexity-aware finite-constellation MIMO detection, and measurement-projection design for nonlinear digital twins. Classical matrix-power bounds are attributed to Berger’s inequality. For a two-state surrogate, Ando semidefinite synthesis is compared with spectral-norm and common-metric Lyapunov synthesis under a shared gain budget; direct spectral-norm minimisation gives the smallest observed amplification. The Crouzeix–Palencia polynomial certificate outperforms stronger classical baselines in only 3 of 300 two-dimensional and 2 of 100 four- and six-dimensional tests. Synthetic 2-by-2 16-QAM detection is evaluated on 10,000 channel frames per SNR with uncertainty intervals. A battery-inspired three-channel sensor model uses an a priori probabilistic noise envelope and a full-rank negative control. Six-state LCL and feeder-restoration studies provide exploratory checks. The findings identify both opportunities and limitations for translating AI-assisted mathematics into electrical engineering through established theory and reproducible numerical studies, without claiming new universal control theorems or physical validation.
